summary: Registry is well-structured and functionally complete with 13 actions across 4 categories. All actions have handlers and icons mapped correctly. No critical bugs found in registry code itself, but weak error handling and platform-specific limitations identified. Quality heavily depends on utils.py (critical bugs documented by scout_4) and team/spawner.py (critical bugs documented by scout_5).

quick_facts.icon_coverage: 100% - all 12 unique icons mapped to Lucide icons

bugs.type: Incomplete error context in subprocess handlers
bugs.issue: Handlers rely on utils.py which swallows all exceptions with broad exception handling and no logging. If subprocess fails (e.g., the agent CLI not installed, permission denied), user sees vague error message with no context about what went wrong.
bugs.example: open_claude_code() (line 111) returns False if any exception occurs. User sees 'Failed to open the agent harness' but can't determine if it's missing binary, wrong path, permission issue, etc.
bugs.impact: Hard to troubleshoot failures. Users cannot self-diagnose setup issues.
bugs.recommendation: Add logging to utils.py functions. Catch specific exceptions in run_action() and provide detailed error messages. Return error_code + error_detail in response.

bugs.type: Multi-step action with weak error handling
bugs.issue: Calls open_vscode_with_claude() AND run_npm_script() sequentially. Both are fire-and-forget subprocess calls. If first succeeds but second fails, returns success=False but VS Code is already open and user is confused.
bugs.details: Line 120: run_npm_script() opens new Windows Terminal tab to run 'npm run dev'. Function returns True if terminal opened, NOT if npm script actually succeeded. If node_modules missing or npm script doesn't exist, user won't know until later.
bugs.impact: User has partial setup (VS Code open but dev server not running). Error message doesn't indicate which component failed.
bugs.recommendation: Either: (1) split into separate actions, or (2) add validation/confirmation that npm actually started before returning success.

bugs.type: Platform limitation not documented at action level
bugs.issue: collapse_team only works on Windows (checks sys.platform != 'win32'). Registry doesn't document this. User on Mac/Linux clicking button gets error 'Only supported on Windows' which is confusing.
bugs.impact: Poor UX. Users don't expect platform-specific actions without clear indication.
bugs.recommendation: Add 'platforms' field to action definition or hide button for non-Windows at frontend level.

bugs.issue: Handler returns {success: True, message, redirect: '/api/server/restart'} but doesn't actually restart server. It delegates to frontend to follow redirect. Returns success=True which is misleading since action isn't complete.
bugs.details: Response format is also non-standard (adds 'redirect' key that other handlers don't use). Frontend must explicitly check for and handle 'redirect' key, but this is implicit/fragile.
bugs.impact: Fragile API contract. If frontend code changes, restart functionality breaks. Success=True is false advertising.
bugs.recommendation: Either: (1) make handler actually restart server (os.kill(os.getpid())), or (2) return success=False with message directing to endpoint.

inconsistencies.issue: Actions handled in two different ways: UI-only (task_list, quick_notes, flight_path, slash_commands, agent_team_builder, stopwatch) vs backend-work (claude_workspace, edgeflow_workspace, explorer_workspace, collapse_team). UI-only actions return immediately (lines 132-153), backend actions call subprocess.
inconsistencies.details: task_list returns 'Opening task list...' without any backend work. claude_workspace calls open_claude_code(). Different execution patterns for conceptually similar actions (both 'open something').
inconsistencies.impact: Unclear API contract. Developers don't know what run_action() actually does without examining code. Hard to reason about which actions are safe to call repeatedly.
inconsistencies.recommendation: Document explicitly in ACTIONS dict which are UI-only. Add 'ui_only: true' flag or create separate ACTIONS_UI and ACTIONS_BACKEND dicts.

inconsistencies.issue: Both edgeflow_workspace (line 25) and software_dev_team (line 80) use 'rocket' icon.
inconsistencies.impact: Reduces visual distinctness in UI. User sees two rocket buttons which is confusing.
inconsistencies.recommendation: Use 'rocket' for 'launch workspace'. Use 'code', 'lightning', or 'zap' for 'build feature'.

inconsistencies.issue: Most actions return {success, message}. restart_server (line 172) adds 'redirect' field. Non-uniform response format.
inconsistencies.impact: Frontend harder to handle uniformly. Some handlers need special-case logic.
inconsistencies.recommendation: Standardize to {success, message, ?data, ?redirect} schema. Document optional fields.

missing_features.type: No action for opening other projects directly
missing_features.issue: Users can open workspace (explorer_workspace) or launch dev workspace, but no dedicated action to open <business> or Legal folders. All project paths hard-coded in PATHS dict.
missing_features.suggestion: Consider parameterized actions like 'open_project(project_name)' or add file browser action.

missing_features.issue: No way to verify action prerequisites are available (the agent CLI installed? npm available? Windows Terminal installed? Folders readable?). Silent failures common.
missing_features.suggestion: Add 'action_health' action that returns {claude: ok|error, npm: ok|error, wt: ok|error, ...}. Or integrate into GET /api/health.

ui_index_html.handler_coverage: All 13 actions have corresponding runAction() handlers
special_cases: mission_control has override wrapper at lines 2843-2849
stopwatch has special spawn logic at lines 677-687

actions_utils_py.issues: Hard-coded paths, command injection vulnerabilities, cross-platform bugs (documented in scout_4_audit)

team_spawner_py.issues: Global state not thread-safe, process handles not retained, race conditions (documented in scout_5_audit)

recommendations.item: Fix utils.py bugs before production: hard-coded paths and command injection vulnerabilities break on other machines. See scout_4_audit.
Fix team/spawner.py bugs: global state not thread-safe, process tracking broken. See scout_5_audit.
Add logging to utils.py. Replace broad 'except Exception: return False' with specific exceptions and detailed logging.
Add try-except to run_action() handlers. Catch subprocess exceptions and return {success: false, error_type, error_message, suggestion}.
Document action metadata: which are UI-only, which require backend, which are platform-specific. Add 'platforms: [win32, darwin, linux]' field.
Standardize response format across all actions. Settle on {success, message, ?data, ?error_type, ?error_detail}.
Add /api/actions/{action_id}/test endpoint that validates prerequisites without executing.
Hide platform-specific actions (e.g., collapse_team) for non-Windows users.

blocking_issues: utils.py hard-coded paths and security vulnerabilities (scout_4)
team/spawner.py global state and race conditions (scout_5)
main_concerns: Silent failures with no logging make debugging difficult
Platform support not documented or handled
Critical bugs in utils.py affect subprocess-based actions
verdict.confidence_level: HIGH - Registry code itself is straightforward. Issues identified are with dependencies and error handling, not registry logic.
